title: Retailers like Wal-Mart and Best Buy are coming up with new strategies to top two-day delivery
summary: Retailers such as Wal-Mart and Best Buy are developing new strategies to surpass the current standard of two-day delivery. Companies are exploring innovative methods for quicker and more efficient delivery to gain a competitive edge. The future of delivery is expected to involve more technology and fewer human laborers, with autonomous vehicles playing a significant role.

title: Not All Moats Are Created Equal
summary: This article analyzes various financial metrics across different moat ratings and sources to understand the fundamental performance investors should expect. It reveals that not all moats are equal, with certain characteristics leading to more attractive financial performance. Key findings include the superior profitability of wide-moat firms, the impact of multiple moat sources, and the standout performance driven by network effect, while efficient scale often leads to narrow moats and less favorable fundamental performance.

title: HP Enterprise Acquires Cloud Technology Partners (CTP); Beware Channel Conflict -
summary: HP Enterprise (HPE) is acquiring Cloud Technology Partners (CTP), a consulting firm specializing in helping Fortune 500 companies migrate workloads to major cloud platforms like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. While CTP's CEO described the acquisition as a logical step after exploring funding options, the deal raises concerns about potential channel conflict for HPE, which recently spun off part of its consulting services. The acquisition brings HPE deeper into consulting, potentially competing with its existing channel and global alliance partners.

title: Disassembling Kodak
summary: This article analyzes Kodak's employment history, comparing its growth trajectory to modern tech giants like Apple, Amazon, and Google. It highlights how long it took Kodak to reach certain employment milestones versus the much faster growth experienced by today's leading tech companies, challenging the narrative that Kodak was a superior "innovation company" compared to Apple.

title: Kroger looks to play the long game against Amazon
summary: Kroger is facing significant competitive pressures, including Amazon's acquisition of Whole Foods and the rise of discounters Aldi and Lidl, which have caused its stock to tumble 35% this year. To combat this, Kroger has implemented strategies like price cuts, internal cost reductions, slowing store growth, and investing in private labels, e-commerce, and store technology, hoping these long-term efforts will improve its financial performance despite near-term headwinds. Analysts anticipate a soft upcoming quarter but believe the grocer's strategic moves position it for future growth amidst a challenging market.

title: The Case For Trian's Nelson Peltz Joining P&G's Board
summary: This article argues for Trian's Nelson Peltz joining Procter & Gamble's board, highlighting P&G's underperformance compared to the S&P 500, its reliance on share buybacks over earnings growth and innovation, and its slow adaptation to changing consumer and marketing trends. Peltz believes P&G needs significant changes in cost-cutting, innovation, and management structure, asserting that the current leadership is not adequately preparing for future market shifts. The piece suggests that shareholders have valid reasons to support Peltz's bid to shake up the company's direction.

title: Amazon opens bidding to cities for $5 billion 'HQ2', a second headquarters
summary: Amazon.com Inc announced it would build a second North American headquarters, dubbed 'HQ2', a $5 billion investment expected to create 50,000 jobs. Cities and states are now bidding for the project, offering tax cuts and incentives. Amazon is seeking a metropolitan area with over a million people, an international airport, good education, and mass transit, with many considering the move a strategy for cost reduction, risk diversification, and access to new talent pools.

title: Kraft Heinz CEO Talks Cost Control, Product Reinvention and People Management
summary: Kraft Heinz CEO Bernardo Hees discusses the company's strategy for growth through cost control, product reinvention, and people management since its formation in 2015. Hees highlights the integration of a meritocratic culture, focusing on performance-driven individuals and adapting to changes in the grocery industry by enhancing product relevance and choices. He also touches on the company's financial improvements and commitment to community involvement.

title: ServiceNow passes security test - now certified to hold AU Govt. info
summary: ServiceNow has achieved Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) certification for cloud services, allowing it to securely hold Australian Government Unclassified DLM information. This certification followed an independent audit of ServiceNow's staff, processes, technology, and Australian data centers, ensuring compliance with stringent government standards. The move is expected to boost confidence for local, state, and federal government agencies considering cloud adoption.

title: Paycom No. 2 among Fortune's fastest-growing companies
summary: Oklahoma City-based Paycom Software Inc. ranked No. 2 on Fortune magazine's 2017 list of 100 fastest-growing companies, making its debut on the list in its first year of eligibility. The ranking is based on three-year growth in revenues, earnings per share, and total stock returns, with Paycom showing significant growth in all these areas. Paycom is the only Oklahoma company and the only software-as-a-service technology provider in its industry to be represented among the top 100.

title: Amazon Plans Mega-Warehouse for Mexico Growth Spurt
summary: Amazon is planning to open a 1 million square-foot warehouse near Mexico City to significantly boost its presence in Mexico's growing e-commerce industry. This expansion aims to triple Amazon's distribution space in Mexico and capitalize on the country's 120 million potential customers, despite challenges like online fraud concerns and a lower e-commerce penetration compared to the U.S. The move comes as talks to revamp NAFTA could potentially benefit Amazon.

title: Office Depot names new marketing chief
summary: Office Depot has appointed Jerri DeVard as executive vice president and chief marketing officer. DeVard will lead the retailer's brand strategy and marketing initiatives, reporting directly to CEO Gerry Smith. This appointment comes as Office Depot focuses on its North America operations and intensifies its marketing efforts following the failed merger with Staples.

title: Arista Networks Makes its Hybrid Cloud Play, Extends EOS
summary: Arista Networks has introduced its Any Cloud software platform, extending its EOS to major public clouds like AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle Cloud, along with Microsoft Azure Stack. The platform integrates the new Arista vEOS Router and CloudVision functionality, including the new Cloud Tracer feature, to provide consistent architecture and operations across hybrid cloud environments. The platform is currently in beta and expected to be generally available on initial public clouds by the end of the year.

title: Lost at Target? If you're on its app, the store knows where you are
summary: Target Corporation is implementing technology that allows its app to track a user's location within a store, displaying it on a store map. This feature aims to help customers navigate the aisles. The article also mentions Target's plan to debut smartphone payment technology in the same year.

title: Albertsons Companies Acquires Plated to Transform the Food Experience for Consumers
summary: Albertsons Companies announced its acquisition of Plated, a meal kit service, to enhance the consumer food experience and scale Plated's business. This acquisition aims to create the first omnichannel meal kit offering with national reach, integrating Plated's technology and chef-designed recipes into Albertsons' stores and digital channels. Plated will operate as a wholly-owned subsidiary, leveraging Albertsons' resources to expand its reach and offerings while maintaining its distinct brand and leadership.

title: Report: Hewlett Packard Enterprise to slash 5,000 jobs, 10% of workforce
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise is reportedly planning to cut 5,000 jobs, representing 10% of its global workforce, by the end of the year. This move follows recent Street-beating third-quarter results and is part of CEO Meg Whitman's strategy to streamline the company and focus on cloud computing and artificial intelligence services. Whitman's commitment to HPE has been reaffirmed despite recent rumors linking her to Uber's CEO search.

title: You can already start applying for holiday jobs
summary: Logistics firms like UPS and FedEx, along with retailers, are preparing to hire thousands of seasonal workers in Indianapolis for the upcoming holiday shopping rush. This hiring trend is particularly strong in warehouse jobs due to the boom in online shopping, with seasonal positions often leading to permanent employment. While brick-and-mortar store closures have reduced some opportunities, analysts see optimism for increased retail hiring due to intense competition and a need to meet consumer demand.

title: Amazon investment to help Shoppers Stop add 25% more stores
summary: Amazon.com Inc.'s investment in Shoppers Stop Ltd. will allow the Indian retailer to boost revenue and add 25 percent more stores, while Amazon expands its reach into smaller Indian towns. Shoppers Stop will raise 1.8 billion rupees ($28 million) by selling a 5 percent stake to Amazon, and the partnership will help Shoppers Stop reach 10% of revenue from online sales by 2020. This deal marks Amazon's first investment in a publicly traded retailer in India.

title: As Amazon takes Whole Foods national, Kroger thinks local
summary: As Amazon-owned Whole Foods scales back its local brand initiatives to centralize operations, Kroger is prioritizing partnerships with local brands across its stores. This strategic move by Kroger aims to attract more local suppliers and consumers, contrasting with Whole Foods' nationalized approach which has seen a drop in foot traffic after an initial Amazon-driven surge. Kroger is also fighting back against stock declines with new initiatives like "comfort food" restaurants and expanding its meal-kit business.

title: Exclusive | BJ’s owner looking to sell chain for $4.5B
summary: BJ’s Wholesale Club's private equity owners, CVC Capital Partners and Leonard Green & Partners, are looking to sell the chain for $4 billion to $4.5 billion, rather than pursuing an IPO. This potential sale aims to provide a significant return on their 2011 investment, which took the company private for $2.8 billion. The owners are currently premarketing the chain to other private equity firms, anticipating a lucrative exit after Amazon's acquisition of Whole Foods disrupted previous sale plans.

title: Kohl’s Will Have a New CEO Next Year
summary: Kohl’s announced that President and CEO Kevin Mansell will retire in May 2018. He will be succeeded by Chief Merchandising and Customer Officer Michelle Gass, with Chief Operating Officer Sona Chawla becoming president. The change comes at a time of significant transformation for brick-and-mortar retailers facing pressure from online competitors.

title: Creating an innovation culture
summary: Waguih Ishak, Corning’s Silicon Valley technology chief, shares insights from his 40-year career on fostering an innovative culture. He emphasizes unconventional strategies like "innovation parenting," encouraging impractical ideas, and cultivating external relationships, rather than just focusing on obvious methods like investment or talent acquisition. The article also highlights the importance of managing project overload, hiring versatile individuals, and breaking hierarchical barriers to promote creativity and successful innovation.

title: Amazon says Google has pulled YouTube from Echo Show device
summary: Amazon announced that Google has inexplicably pulled YouTube from its Echo Show devices, causing a rare public dispute between the two tech giants. Google countered that Amazon's implementation of YouTube violated its terms of service, leading to a "broken user experience." This incident affects the Echo Show's video content and highlights ongoing competitive tensions in Silicon Valley.

title: Life360 Launches Beta Notifications Skill for Amazon Alexa
summary: Life360 has launched a new beta Notifications Skill for Amazon Alexa, allowing users to receive real-time location alerts and updates on their family members directly through their Alexa-enabled devices. This new feature provides an additional way for Life360 users to stay informed about their family's whereabouts and safety without needing to check their phones. The skill integrates Life360's existing location sharing capabilities with Alexa's voice assistant technology.
